Executive Summary: 

(a) The Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policy: 
Inland Fuel Terminals, Incorporated (Inland) operates the Inland Bridgeport Terminal with a goal of preventing the accidental release of propane through a comprehensive accidental release prevention and emergency response program.   The major components of the program include meeting and/or exceeding legal and regulatory requirements, an overall environmental, safety, and health management system, terminal operating procedures, and personnel training.  Inland works closely with emergency responders, the public, and the local community to ensure an effective emergency response plan is in place.

(b) The Stationary Source and Substance Handled: 
The Inland Bridgeport Terminal is owned by Inland Fuel Terminals, Incorporated, with headquarters in Bridgeport, CT. At this terminal, tank trucks of propane are off-loaded into a bulk storage tank.  As needed, the propane is taken out of the bulk tank and loaded into tank trucks for off-site delivery. Propane is the Chemical Accident Prevention (CAP) regulated chemical stored at the terminal which exceeds a threshold quantity.

(c) General Accidental Release Prevention Program and Chemical-Specific Prevention Steps:  
The Inland Bridgeport Terminal is a secure facility which is manned during normal business hours (only approved truckers can perform loading and unloading during other hours). The terminal is regulated as a Program 3 process.  
The facility has developed an accident release prevention program and implemented chemical general accidental release prevention programs and propane-specific release prevention steps for the covered process. The program includes both a documented compliance manual and administrative procedures to manage the program.  Specific elements of the program include:
- Documented management system
-Routine hazard assessments, including an offsite consequence analysis
-Process hazard analysis program, to eva

luate controls and safeguards of the process
-Written standard operating procedures for inventory management and operations
-Written training program for the risk management program, inclusive of applicable operating, maintenance, and emergency response procedures
-Mechanical integrity program, including internal and external/contractor duties
-Management of change process, to evaluate changes
-Pre-startup safety review process, to review applicable changes
-Routine compliance audit program, inclusive of third-party audits (as applicable)
-Written incident investigation program, inclusive of corrective actions
-Written employee participation program, to involve applicable employees
-Hot work program, inclusive of hot work permits
-Contractor selection (and evaluation) program
-Written emergency response/action program
-Document risk management plan
In addition to the covered process (and accidental release prevention program), the facility has active safety programs involving all site personnel.  All employees have the authority to stop work if deemed unsafe and report the unsafe condition to their supervisor(s).
New employees (and drivers) receive facility-specific training.  Additionally, facility personnel received ongoing safety training, including Hazardous Waste Operations and Emergency Response (HAZWOPER) training.

(d) Five Year Accident History:  
There have been no accidental releases, with known offsite impacts, meeting the definition contained in 40 CFR §68.42(a) within the last five years of operation. 

NOTE: A non-reportable incident occurred on August 03, 2022. There were no on-site deaths, injuries (beyond first aid or involving missed work), or significant property damage. Additionally, there were no known offsite deaths, injuries, property damage, environmental damage, evacuations, or sheltering in place.

(e) Emergency Response Program and Exercises:
NOTE: The facility is considered a non-responding stationary source for propane releases, per 4

0 CFR  §68.90(b)
The facility has developed an Emergency Action Plan.  The plan addresses fires/explosions, spills/releases of hazardous chemicals, and other potential emergency conditions.  The plan details response actions by facility personnel for such emergencies, safety and emergency equipment, communication responsibilities, and coordination with offsite responders (including notification to local, state, and federal agencies).
Should an emergency release of propane occur at the facility, the facility will be evacuated.  The Bridgeport Fire Department will be notified, and the Fire Department will assume Incident Command.
Notification Exercises:  Annually, Inland coordinates emergency response duties (or actions) with the Fire Department through a meeting.  Meetings include an attendance roster/sign-in sheet.  A memorandum of understation (or other summary document) will be developed for future exercises.

(f) Planned Changes to Improve Safety:  
As a result of the recent compliance audit (and ongoing process hazard analysis), a number of improvements to the risk management program have either been completed or are planned. Improvements are intended to improve the safety of the process and minimize the potential for release. Changes primarily include program changes (improved documentation), operating procedures or checklist updates, and employee training.

Registration:

Offsite Consequence Analysis:
As a Program Level 3 covered process with a regulated flammable substance, an offsite consequence analysis (OCA) has been performed for one worst-case release scenario and one alternative release scenario.  The required data from the OCA is contained within this Risk Management Plan.
